completion_promises.evidence: TestBridgeFirstThenSyncRaiseSkipsSafetyNet.test_bridge_claim_then_safety_net_skip — first calls ledger.claim(claimed_by=CLAIMER_BRIDGE_TERMINAL) (returns True), then awaits the production wrapper _build_publish_build_failed(publisher, terminal_publish_ledger=ledger). The wrapper consults the ledger via TerminalPublishLedger.claim and observes claim()==False, so it short-circuits without invoking publisher.publish_build_failed. Test asserts publisher.publish_build_failed.assert_not_awaited() and that the ledger row's claimed_by is still CLAIMER_BRIDGE_TERMINAL. Production wiring: _build_publish_build_failed in src/forge/cli/_serve_deps.py now accepts terminal_publish_ledger and runs the claim before attach_correlation_id+publish.

completion_promises.criterion_text: A first-wins invariant test asserts no race condition can produce two terminal envelopes for the same build, regardless of ordering: bridge-first / F010F-first / concurrent.
completion_promises.evidence: TestFirstWinsInvariant has three sub-tests: test_bridge_first_then_safety_net_publishes_zero (bridge wins → wrapper skips, publisher.publish_build_failed not awaited), test_safety_net_first_then_bridge_claim_loses (F010F wins → wrapper publishes once, subsequent ledger.claim returns False so the bridge would skip), test_concurrent_gather_produces_exactly_one_envelope (asyncio.gather on bridge_publish + f010f_publish coroutines; total envelopes from both paths summed to exactly 1, plus a SQL COUNT(*) over the ledger asserts a single row). The first-wins invariant rests on the atomic BEGIN IMMEDIATE + INSERT OR IGNORE in TerminalPublishLedger.claim — the row's composite PRIMARY KEY (feature_id, correlation_id) means SQLite enforces uniqueness at insert time and rowcount==1 only for the winner.
